pages.imagePrompt: Blossom Meadow fair sign-up table with clipboard full of names. Gulu squirrel reading list, ears drooping slightly. Spring Fair bustle in background.
pages.text:
The fair list was full of names — Mimi, Bobo, Kiki, Timo, Pip.

Gulu the squirrel read it twice. He traced each line with one claw.

His name wasn't there. Not once.

pages.imagePrompt: Gulu watching friends at tasks — Mimi humming with ribbons, Bobo chatting, Kiki flying errands. Gulu standing alone with empty paws.
pages.text:
Mimi hummed while she folded ribbons. Bobo told the mud story again — making friends laugh on purpose this time.

Kiki flew errands with a list in her beak.

Gulu had nothing in his paws. No job. No line on the board.

pages.imagePrompt: Gulu walking away from busy fair toward distant Tree of Wisdom. Small figure, big tree ahead, quiet path.
pages.text:
Gulu's tummy felt hollow — not hungry, just empty.

He didn't stomp. He didn't shout.

He walked toward the Tree of Wisdom and sat down without a word.

pages.imagePrompt: Gulu sitting under great Tree of Wisdom, fair noise distant and soft. Bark patterns, dappled light, peaceful stillness.
pages.text:
The Tree was old and wide. Its branches made a quiet roof.

From here, the fair sounded far away — drums, voices, clapping — like a song through a closed door.

Gulu hugged his knees. He didn't know what to do next.

pages.imagePrompt: Guru Ma Owl in tree nook above, soft grey feathers, kind eyes, listening posture — not preaching. Gulu below looking up.
pages.text:
Above, in the Tree's nook, Guru Ma Owl opened one eye.

She didn't fly down with a speech. She didn't fix the list.

She listened.

pages.imagePrompt: Close-up Gulu speaking up to tree, vulnerable expression. Owl listening from nook, warm lamplight glow.
pages.text:
"I don't know what to do," Gulu said. His voice came out small. "Everyone has a job. I don't."

The fair kept humming in the distance.

Gulu waited. He didn't make up a brave answer.

pages.imagePrompt: Guru Ma Owl gentle smile from nook, Gulu below still sitting — honest surrender moment, no lecture.
pages.text:
Guru Ma Owl was quiet for a long moment.

Then she said, "That's honest."

Gulu's ears lifted — just a little. Being honest didn't feel like failing. It felt like telling the truth.

pages.imagePrompt: Gulu standing slowly under tree, looking toward distant flower table with empty water pitchers. One small choice forming.
pages.text:
Gulu looked toward the meadow. Near the flower table, pitchers sat empty. No one was carrying water.

His paws itched to help — but he still didn't know the big answer.

Maybe he could do one small yes.

pages.imagePrompt: Gulu carrying water pitcher to flower table, careful steps. Mimi glancing over with grateful smile. Modest helpful action.
pages.text:
Gulu picked up a pitcher. It was heavy — but not too heavy.

He carried water to the flower table. Once. Then again.

Mimi looked up. "Oh — thank you, Gulu."

"I still don't know my big job," Gulu said. "But I can carry water today."

pages.imagePrompt: Gulu filling pitchers at table, flowers bright, fair continuing around him. Timo nodding as he passes. Quiet belonging.
pages.text:
Timo passed with nails for a repair. "Slow and steady," he said — and meant it as praise.

Gulu filled the pitchers. The flowers drank. The fair kept going.

He wasn't on the big list yet. He was here anyway.

pages.imagePrompt: Gulu and friends at dusk near Tree of Wisdom, four leaves on branch implied in background art. Spring Fair week winding down.
pages.text:
At dusk, Kiki flew down. "You found a yes," she said.

Gulu nodded. "A small one."

"Small counts," Kiki said — and for once, she didn't rush away.

pages.imagePrompt: Gulu under Tree of Wisdom at twilight, Guru Ma Owl nook glowing softly. Peaceful close to Spring Fair week.
pages.text:
Gulu sat under the Tree one more minute.

He still didn't know everything. But he had said so — out loud — and chosen one step.

Spring Fair week had room for that kind of honest too.
